intended_object: The canonical monomorphism 𝒩_X ↪ 𝒪_X of sheaves of 𝒪_X-modules, where 𝒩_X is the nilradical ideal sheaf of the scheme X (taken from the docstring and name).
explanation:
The definition is just `X.nilradical.toModuleι`. `X.nilradical` is Mathlib's nilradical `IdealSheafData`, which is the radical of the zero ideal sheaf. `toModuleι` is the inclusion `I.toSubmodule.ι` into the unit sheaf of modules 𝒪_X. Here `I.toSubmodule` is the kernel, open set by open set, of the map 𝒪_X → ι_*𝒪_Z, where Z is the closed subscheme cut out by I. That kernel is the ideal sheaf I itself. The library also proves that on affine opens the sections of this module are the nilradical of Γ(X, U). So the morphism is exactly the inclusion of the nilradical ideal sheaf into the structure sheaf.

The construction applies to any scheme, so there is no issue of generality. Mathlib has the nilradical only as `IdealSheafData`. As far as I found, it does not package an ideal sheaf as an 𝒪_X-module with its inclusion map, so there is no Mathlib counterpart to cite.
